chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “Whoever follows a جنازة, four qirats are written for him: one qirat for following it, one qirat for performing salat over it, one qirat for waiting until its burial is completed, and one qirat for offering condolences.”

key_terms.بِالصَّلَاةِ: by performing salat over the deceased
key_terms.جَنَازَةً: the funeral bier or funeral procession of the deceased
key_terms.دَفْنِهَا: its burial, meaning the interment of the deceased
key_terms.قَرَارِيطَ: units of reward granted for these acts
key_terms.قِيرَاطٌ: a measured share of divine reward
key_terms.لِلتَّعْزِيَةِ: for offering condolences to the bereaved

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for following a funeral procession and offering condolences in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the merit of participating fully in funeral rites and supporting the bereaved. It presents multiple stages of accompanying the deceased and consoling the family as rewarded acts, emphasizing communal responsibility and compassion around death.
